data.value: First-time setup: The default idle threshold is 20 minutes. Reminders after sleep depend on your PC’s sleep mode and system policy. Test this on your PC first. data.value: This filter is off by default. Enable it only after confirming that events without a device ID are interfering. It may miss some touchpad or remote input. Use it only with verified external keyboards and mice. A device ID does not guarantee a physical device. On this PC, an elevated game required matching privileges to receive real input. A non-elevated reminder falls back when the foreground app has higher privileges and shows a warning. Saving device event mode requests normal UAC if needed; startup checks too. Canceling keeps the app running without elevation and retains the fallback. If no UAC prompt appears after enabling device timing, try Save Settings again and dismiss the saved message. An already elevated app will not request permission again.

data.name: SettingsForm_030
data.value: Device event timing helps when a game or another app keeps resetting the system input timer. It counts keyboard and mouse event headers only. It does not read key contents or pointer coordinates, or install hooks. Virtual devices, touch, remote control, and anti-cheat compatibility remain limited. Device events are not guaranteed to represent physical input. If input cannot be received, timing falls back to Windows. Lock-screen, sleep, slideshow, and pause rules still apply. Saving settings or changing modes restarts idle counting.

data.value: Automatic volume boost: configure each separate speaker on Device Volume. Settings, imported audio, and size-limited diagnostic logs are stored in the project's data folder. data.name: MediaScopePanel_015
data.value: Lower only listed players with active audio. Keeping media playing does not prevent volume reduction. Music can be reduced even when media pausing is off. The pause scope and exception list above do not block these volume changes. Browser audio is handled per app, not per URL. Volume is restored afterward; manual app-volume or mute changes are kept. Enabling reduction also selects permission for master-volume boost. You can clear that permission separately. Playback continues. Coordinated boost also requires an enabled, confirmed device target on Device Volume. When master volume rises, music on the same device is reduced further to compensate for the actual gain in decibels. Music may briefly mute during the transition to avoid an initial volume spike. Allowing boost may also make other, unlisted audio louder. At the end, master volume is restored first, then player volume. Normal previews do not trigger this.

data.name: DeviceVolumePanel_012Details
data.value: Only volume below the target is raised. Existing higher volume is not reduced; muted devices are not unmuted. Volume is restored afterward. Manual volume or mute changes during playback are kept. Changing master volume during a reminder can suddenly make reduced media louder. Device names and drivers cannot verify physical connections. Do not enable this for shared jacks.

data.name: DeviceVolumePanel_012Tail
data.value: Normal preview buttons do not adjust master volume. After confirmation, enable the option and save.

data.name: MediaScopePanel_016Details
data.value: Browsers are handled as whole apps. URLs and tabs cannot be distinguished reliably. URL lists are unsupported. Web pages, history, and media titles are not read. An empty list in listed-apps-only mode pauses no media. Pause and volume reduction lists are saved separately. Neither list determines whether a reminder plays. Without coordinated boost permission, other active, unreduced audio blocks master-volume boost.

data.name: PhonePanel_010Details
data.value: Notifications are sent asynchronously after reminder playback actually begins. Offline phones or delivery failures do not affect PC playback. Expired notifications are not sent after reconnection.

data.name: SlideShowPanel_003Details
data.value: A running app or an arbitrary full-screen window is not enough to identify a slideshow. Slides, document names, window titles, notes, and screen contents are not read. After a show ends, reminders follow actual idle time. Missed reminders are not queued. Existing running-app suppression rules still apply. Remove conflicting rules.

data.name: SuppressionPanel_011Details
data.value: Browse Apps is for running rules only. Playing rules use Windows media sessions for both music and video. They do not distinguish URLs. Running rules check whether an EXE is running, including in the background or minimized. No process memory is read. A browser rule can affect the whole browser. Choose carefully. If detection fails, normal idle rules apply. Checks run about every 2 seconds. After a rule stops matching, reminders follow actual idle time. Missed reminders are not queued.

data.name: SuppressionPanel_011Tail
data.value: Remove a rule to restore normal detection for that app. Save after editing.
